status: corrective source audit; implementation and live proof not performed

notation.anchors: Prefix aliases resolve through sources; all line ranges are inclusive. J is primary, E/C corroborate reachability, R/D prove current Rust behavior.
notation.fields: Ordered payload only, not ISAAC opcode or -1/-2 frame length prefix. u8/i8/u16/i16/i32/u64 are ordinary big-endian reads without add/sub/neg/LE transforms. str10 is newline-terminated string. bits(n) is MSB-first. uSmart = u8 if peek<128 else u16-32768. Empty array means truly zero payload.
notation.legacy: [274 wire ID, semantic name, actual dispatch/handler anchors]; not a constant-only mapping. null means no equivalent implementation in the audited 274 Rust dispatcher.
notation.gens: [current R289 successful-packet family, required family]. none means no family bump, not no state mutation. T1/T2/logout invalidate all. Explicit family contract is in cleanup plan; R:3722-3813 supplies current mapping.
notation.verdict: missing=no top-level R289 implementation; partial=implemented but identified semantic/publication/framing gap; complete=source semantics and existing family behavior accounted for, not proof of live compatibility. Every nonempty row also inherits F1 framing defect unless its note explicitly identifies an exact-end implementation.
notation.reach: Conservative operation-level reachability, not a claim that every condition ran during a particular login. Each ID names engine emission/command edges; representative content witnesses below establish conditional categories. No actual fixture exclusions are asserted. Direct zone and enclosed-zone coverage are separate.

cross_cutting_findings.F1: R:3628-3688 bounds socket read by reusable Packet allocation, not semantic reads by psize; R:3699-3711 has no universal exact-end check. str10/fixed reads can read old allocation bytes beyond frame, and trailing payload is accepted. Catching allocation OOB is not strict framing. New R289 decoder must use bounded frame and validate before publication.
cross_cutting_findings.F2: R:3722-3742 only bumps inv/player/npc/varp/chat-filter/rebuild. Successfully handled widgets, stats, message-game, camera-reset and zone frames omit their matching 274 generations; duplicate ID-based family switches are unsafe.
cross_cutting_findings.F3: R:7857-7859 silently discards rest of enclosed frame on unknown inner opcode and reports success. Direct zone packets never route to zone_packet_289. Java supports eleven zone operations, not the ten copied from engine table.
cross_cutting_findings.F4: R:6802-6808 consumes LAST_LOGIN_INFO but never publishes fields or opens welcome interface. The 274 branch R:6288-6290 is also a no-op; not parity-complete.
cross_cutting_findings.F5: Actor wire layouts largely match but primary health-bar timeout is cycle+300 (J:5177,5251,11881,11928), shared Rust is +400. Preserve 274 +400; implement explicit R289 +300. Source-proven difference is not erased by existing goldens.
cross_cutting_findings.F6: Existing protocol-289.json outbound EVENT_MOUSE_CLICK incorrectly says two u16 coordinates. J:5882-5907 emits one packed i32 timestamp/button/coordinate. Camera193 is pitch then yaw, not yaw then pitch. This audit supersedes those field claims; constant map does not mean actual emitter exists.
cross_cutting_findings.F7: J:1819-1835 publishes tutorial message text and clears click for kind0 with tutorial component open. R:4178-4196 explicitly omits it. R:4203-4235 also lacks J:3264-3276 chalreq parsing. These are behavior gaps shared with legacy, requiring explicit R289 treatment.

outbound_contract.row_format: Each row includes actual emit anchors, not declaration hits. legacy is the public 274 semantic constant passed at those same R/D sites; map_client_prot in crates/client/src/io/client_prot_289.rs:149-235 selects 289 without changing payload. Fields below exclude variable-frame size prefixes. p1/p2/p3/p4/p8 mean big-endian widths. A missing emit is a capability gap even though the constant maps.
outbound_contract.verdicts: mapped = source layout agrees with current emit, not a live claim; partial = named behavioral difference; missing = no R/D emitter. Fields are payload order; values outside representable signed widths use ordinary low-byte serialization.
outbound_contract.movement: R:3541-3583 and J:10154-10196: at most25 turns, p1 run, p2 first absolute X,Z, signed p1 pairs relative to first turn; minimap appends14 bytes. All three use -1 framing. Shared legacy encoder; no endian transform.
outbound_contract.omissions: No production emit sites for IDLE_TIMER, EVENT_MOUSE_CLICK/MOVE/APPLET_FOCUS/CAMERA_POSITION, CYCLELOGIC4/5/7. These are missing in both Rust revisions, not eight successfully mapped behaviors. Camera Java writes pitch then yaw (J:5918-5920), contrary to old protocol-289.json labels. Mouse click is packed p4, not two coordinates. Implement missing lifecycle/input paths for 289 explicitly, not by adding constants.
outbound_contract.legacy_differences: MESSAGE_PUBLIC has explicit R289 colour/effect support R:8922-8954; SEND_SNAPSHOT uses REPORT_ABUSE semantic with R289-only name/reason/mute framing R:4889-4907. Cyclelogic2 uses deterministic valid choices rather than Java random choices; do not describe randomness parity. Other mapped rows retain shared 274 ordered payload as named below.
